# Who's Afraid of A.I. Music? (The New Yorker)

By Kelefa Sanneh. Published in The New Yorker, 2026-09-07 issue (online Aug 31, 2026).

## Key findings
- **Fenix Flexin** (L.A. rapper, member of Shoreline Mafia) released the '80s UK synth-pop single **"Rubberz"** in June 2026; it went viral and peaked at **No. 58 on the Billboard Hot 100**.
- Listeners suspected the song was created with **AI** (the voice/accent didn't match his usual style). Fenix initially denied it ("No AI on it"), then after producer **Medasin** posted a breakdown arguing it was made with the AI tool **Treblo** (formerly Sonauto) — and Treblo released a detector labeling "Rubberz" "very likely Treblo" — Fenix stopped denying it: "Never said I didn't use AI... ain't nothing wrong w using new technology as a tool."
- The piece frames "Rubberz" as a viral AI-assisted hip-hop moment and ties it to the broader summer 2026 AI-in-music backlash (also mentions Tyga's $tarface and his Pitchfork 0.0 review).

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — The New Yorker is a top-tier outlet.
- Establishes: Fenix Flexin (human rapper) is the artist behind the viral AI-assisted (Treblo) hit "Rubberz" (No. 58 Billboard Hot 100, June 2026); he initially denied, then conceded AI use. Caveat: the AI-generation of the vocals is the subject of the controversy; Fenix's own involvement in the vocal is disputed (live performances show him unable to reproduce the recorded voice/accent).
